text:
maria: Heads-up: after last kernel patch in eu-west-1 I'm seeing a spike of GPU pods Pending/Init. Node-level device-plugin logs show advertise() happening before nvidia modules are present, so scheduler put workloads on nodes without /dev/nvidia0. lots of evictions and slow scheduling backpressure.

lee: Can you paste the node/pod outputs? which k8s version and the kernel version rolled?

maria: k8s 1.26, kernel 6.1.0-rc1 variant from our image build. example: 
```
$ kubectl get pods -n ml -o wide | grep gpu
ml-train-7f6d9 Pending 0/1 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient gpu.
$ kubectl describe node ip-10-0-5-12
Conditions: Ready True
Annotations: device-plugin.advertised=true
Events:	Registered device plugin: nvidia-device-plugin v0.12
```
But on that node: 
```
$ ls /dev | grep nvidia || echo no-dev
no-dev
$ sudo lsmod | grep nvidia || true
(no output)
$ journalctl -u kubelet | grep device-plugin
I0912 12:01:23 DevicePlugin: advertising capacity 4 GPUs
I0912 12:01:24 probe: modprobe returned ENOENT
```

sam: Looks like module load ordering changed (dkms/kernel packaging). DevicePlugin starts as a DaemonSet and advertises quickly — we rely on either /dev or a probe. New kernels expose module aliases later, so modprobe is deferred.

olivia: Short-term: we can patch the device-plugin DS to set advertise=false until the node has /dev/nvidia0 present (there's a config flag in upstream plugin). Or add a preStart hook that waits for module.

sam: Minimal workaround I tried locally: edit the daemonset args: `--fail-on-no-dev=false --advertise=false` then trigger rollout. That prevented new adverts; scheduler stopped assigning GPUs to those nodes.

maria: Can we roll that to eu-west-1 canary? We have 20 nodes affected but only ~4 running jobs so low user impact if canary is small.

deploy-bot: Started rolling patch to ds/nvidia-device-plugin in namespace kube-system (canary nodes: ip-10-0-5-12, ip-10-0-5-15).

lee: Also flagging cluster autoscaler behaviour — it sees insufficient gpu and tries to scale but node filters rely on advertised capacity and we end up in a loop. For now scale-down disabled in eu-west-1 to avoid churn.

sam: Long-term: we should change the operator probe to use udev events or check /sys/module/<mod>/taint rather than modprobe timing. Also add a startup readiness gate for device-plugin that waits for a small udev rule. I can draft a PR.

olivia: Agree. I'll open an RFC about changing probe approach + add a canary rollout plan. Also putting a checklist to avoid rolling kernel images during production TF job windows.

maria: Action items:
- olivia: open PR + canary plan (IN-PROG)
- sam: prototype readiness gate + udev-based probe (IN-PROG)
- lee: keep scale-down off in eu-west and coordinate migration of 2 big training jobs to us-west for next 4hrs
- ops: rolling restart of plugin DS scheduled 00:00 UTC (canary first)

sam: snippet I used to detect device correctly: 
```bash
# wait-for-nvidia.sh (simple)
for i in {1..30}; do
  if [ -e /dev/nvidia0 ]; then exit 0; fi
  sleep 1
done
exit 2
```
This is ugly but effective. We'll replace with event-driven approach.

maria: Thanks. note: cost impact — we temporarily bumped Dedicated pool in us-west by +2 gpus to absorb jobs; finance FYI (cc:billing) — expect ~300USD/day until next Tuesday.

olivia: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gpu-operator/pull/432 - includes advertise toggle and a readiness hook. will link tests.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout succeeded on 2 nodes. No new failed adverts in last 10m.

lee: Monitoring: queue length decreased, evictions stopped. we'll keep watch until midnight then full rollout if stable.

maria: Great. please avoid further kernel pushes in eu-west until we validate the fix. :white_check_mark:
